name: ServiceNow
description: ServiceNow sells cloud software that automates work inside large companies: IT help desks first, then customer service, HR, legal, procurement, security operations and a platform to build custom workflow apps. Customers (about 8,700 at end of 2025) sign multi-year subscription contracts, mostly annual billing, which is 97% of revenue; the rest is implementation services. It has moved into AI and security through purchases in the past nine months: Moveworks ($2.4B, closed December 2025), Veza ($1.2B, March 2026) and Armis ($7.6B cash, April 2026). Split 5 for 1 in December 2025. GAAP operating margin fell to about 4% in Q2 2026 while the company-adjusted margin stayed near 30%.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recalled from the standard scheme and uncertain; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source.

hq.note: 2225 Lawson Lane, Santa Clara (search coverage of the FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Subscription
businessLines.how: Annual or multi-year subscriptions priced by user, product and increasingly consumption of AI actions; customers expand by adding workflows, which is why the company tracks large contracts.
businessLines.description: Four product areas: Technology Workflows (IT operations, service management, risk, security), CRM and Industry Workflows (customer, field service, sales and order management), Core Business Workflows (HR, legal, procurement, workplace) and Creator and Other (App Engine, data infrastructure). Revenue by product area was not extracted.

businessLines.name: Professional services and other
businessLines.how: One-time fees for deploying and training customers on the platform; a small, low-margin add-on to subscriptions.

brands.name: Moveworks
brands.note: Enterprise search and virtual agents; $2.4B ($1.467B stock, $905M cash); closed 2025-12-15

brands.name: Veza
brands.note: AI identity security; about $1.2B cash; closed 2026-03-02

brands.name: Armis
brands.note: Cyber-exposure and cyber-physical security; about $7.6B cash; closed 2026-04-20
